'''Ronny Hadani''' ({{Langx|he|רוני הדני}}) is an [[Israeli-American]] mathematician, specializing in representation theory and harmonic analysis, with applications to signal processing.<ref name="Alumni">{{cite web |url=https://www.weizmann.ac.il/math/alumni/M.Sc.%20Students |title=Alumni |publisher=The Weizmann Institute of Science Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science |access-date=July 29, 2020 }}</ref><ref name="IEEE Conference">{{cite web |url=http://www.ieeevtc.org/vtc2018fall/final-program.pdf |title=The 88th IEEE Vehicular Technology Conference |publisher=IEEE |access-date=September 24, 2020 |date=2018}}</ref>   He is known for developing [[Orthogonal Time Frequency and Space (OTFS)]] modulating techniques, a method used for making wireless [[5G]] communications faster,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://engineering.nyu.edu/academics/departments/electrical-and-computer-engineering/seminars-fall-2017#OTF |title=Seminars: Fall 2017 |publisher=NYU Tandon School of Engineering|access-date=September 24, 2020 |date=2017}}</ref> that is also being considered for use in [[6G (network)|6G]] technology.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.6gworld.com/exclusives/the-otfs-interview-implications-of-a-6g-candidate-technology/ |last=Lawrence|first=Alex|title=The OTFS Interview – Implications of a 6G Candidate Technology|publisher=6G World|access-date=September 24, 2020 |date=December 9, 2020}}</ref> The technology is being used by several wireless [[5G]] related companies and Cohere Technologies, a company he has co-founded.<ref name="5G World">{{cite web |url=http://bsp-5gworld-2016.nettools1.tf.informatm.com/company/cohere-technologies/ |title=Cohere Technologies |publisher=5G World|access-date=September 24, 2020}}</ref><ref name="Qualcomm">{{cite web|title=Seminar Series: Ronny Hadani|url=https://qi.ucsd.edu/events/event.php?id=2952&go=newer|access-date=September 24, 2020|publisher=Qualcomm Institute}}</ref><ref name="Justia" /><ref name="Cryo-Electron">{{cite journal |last1=Hadani |first1=Ronny |last2=Singer |first2=Amit |date=1 September 2011 |title=Representation theoretic patterns in three dimensional Cryo-Electron Microscopy I: The intrinsic reconstitution algorithm |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=174 |issue=2 |pages=1219–1241 |doi= 10.4007/annals.2011.174.2.11|pmid=23180881 |pmc=3505076 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=UIaOM7MAAAAJ|title=Shamgar Gurevich |website=Google Scholar|access-date=September 25, 2020}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Hadani received his MS degree in Computer Science from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in 1999 under the supervision of [[David Harel]]. He received his Ph.D. degree in Pure Mathematics from [[Tel-Aviv University]] in 2006 under the supervision of [[Joseph Bernstein]].<ref name="Alumni" /><ref name="IEEE Conference" />

==Career==
===Academia===
From the years 2006 to 2009, Hadani held an L.E. Dickson Postdoctoral Fellowship of Mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]]. Since 2009, he has been an associate professor of mathematics at the [[University of Texas, Austin]].<ref name="IEEE Conference" /><ref name="W08">{{cite web |url=https://icc2019.ieee-icc.org/workshop/w08-wireless-communications-high-mobility/program|title=W08: Wireless Communications in High Mobility |date=5 November 2018 |publisher=IEEE|access-date=September 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cns.utexas.edu/directory/item/15-mathematics/354-hadani-ronny?Itemid=349|title=Directory: Ronny Hadani |publisher=University of Texas at Austin|access-date=September 24, 2020}}</ref>

===Cohere Technologies===
In 2010, Hadani co-founded Cohere Technologies with Shlomo Rakib. The company is a Silicon Valley wireless startup that focuses on wireless improvements using OTFS and the Delay-Doppler model to improve FDD/TDD spectrum performance with channel detection, estimation, prediction, and precoding software for [[4G LTE|4G]] and [[5G]] networks, compliant with 3GPP standards and O-RAN.<ref name="5G World" /><ref name="W08" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cns.utexas.edu/news/ronny-hadani-comes-in-loud-and-clear|title=Ronny Hadani Comes in Loud and Clear |publisher=The University of Texas at Austin College of Natural Sciences|access-date=September 24, 2020}}</ref>

In December 2022, during the inaugural 6G Evolution Summit event opening keynote, [[Fierce Wireless]] moderator referred to Hadani as “The Father of OTFS.”<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-12 |title=6G Evolution Summit event opening keynote |url=https://onlinexperiences.com/scripts/Server.nxp?LASCmd=L:0&AI=1&ShowKey=211506&LoginType=0&InitialDisplay=1&ClientBrowser=0&DisplayItem=NULL&LangLocaleID=0&SSO=1&RFR=https://onlinexperiences.com/launch/event.htm?showkey=211506 |access-date=2023-02-10 |website=onlinexperiences.com}}</ref>

==Patents==
Hadani has been granted over 70 OTFS related patents, which include a communications method employing Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) shifting and spectral shaping, which allows users to transmit and receive at least one frame of data ([D]) over a wireless communications link. He has also patented methods of operating and implementing wireless OTFS communications systems.<ref name="Justia">{{cite web |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/ronny-hadani|title=Patents by Inventor Ronny Hadani |publisher=Justia Patents|website=patents.justia.com|access-date=September 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
